idea.body: A series adds up every term of a sequence. Sigma notation writes that sum compactly. The sum from k = 1 to 4 of 2k + 1 means add up 2k + 1 for every k from 1 to 4. That is 3 + 5 + 7 + 9, which is 24. An arithmetic series has the shortcut n/2 times (first term plus last term). A geometric series has the shortcut a_1 times (r^n - 1)/(r - 1). When a geometric series keeps going forever with a ratio smaller than 1 in size, it still settles on one exact number, a_1/(1 - r). A telescoping sum is a different trick. Its terms split apart so that most of them cancel, leaving only a few pieces standing.

figure.alt: A row of boxes for the sequence 3, 5, 7, 9, with a plus sign implied between them, summing to 24.

workedExample.prompt:
A savings jar starts with 10 dollars and gets 5 more dollars every week.
What is the running total after 6 weeks, including the start?
steps: This is an arithmetic series with a_1 = 10 and common difference 5.
The running total after 6 weeks is 135 dollars.

figure.alt: A row of boxes for the weekly amounts, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35.

ways.name: Write and read sigma notation
ways.when: Use this to write sums compactly or expand a sum from sigma notation.
steps: Sigma notation: sum from k = 1 to 4 of 2k + 1.
ways.example: sum from k = 1 to 4 of 2k + 1. What is the sum?
ways.trap: Forgetting to plug in every value of k or adding terms with the wrong expression.

ways.name: The arithmetic sum formula
ways.when: Use this shortcut when adding an arithmetic sequence.
steps: Sum = n/2 times (first plus last) = 5/2 times (2 + 14) = 2.5 times 16 = 40.
No need to add each term one by one.
ways.trap: Using the formula with wrong first or last term, or forgetting the n/2 factor.

ways.name: Pair the ends like Gauss
ways.when: Use this to see why the arithmetic sum formula works.
steps: Five pairs, each sum 11, so 5 times 11 = 55.
That is n/2 times (first plus last).
ways.trap: Forgetting to pair opposite ends or counting the pairs wrong.

figure.alt: Two rows showing numbers 1 to 10 and 10 to 1, with sums between them.

frames.caption: Pair the ends: each pair sums to 11.
That is n/2 times (first plus last).
